reconstruction: Two distinct targets are linked. (1) For every type α with Nonempty α and Countable α and every indexed family C : Nat → Set α, a semantic identifier exists if and only if each index i has a finite tell-tale T_i⊆C i satisfying: for every j, T_i⊆C j and C j⊆C i imply C i⊆C j. For fixed C, one total function M : List α → Nat must work for all target indices z and all streams s : Nat → α with range(s)=C z. For each (z,s), there exist k and N, possibly depending on z and the whole stream as well as C and M, such that C k=C z and for every t≥N, M([s(0),…,s(t−1)])=k. The final index k need not equal z. This is eventual stability of a single natural-number name, with no rate or bound on N. Empty family members are allowed in this semantic target. (2) For every EffectiveIndexedFamily F on Nat, EffectiveInferrable F is equivalent to ConditionOne F: there exists one total jointly computable emit : Nat → Nat → Option Nat whose emitted set E_i={x | ∃stage, emit i stage=some x} is finite for each i, lies in F.language i, and satisfies the same tell-tale exclusion property. EffectiveInferrable adds Computable M to the identifier property. F packages a total uniformly computable exact Boolean membership function and nonemptiness of every indexed language.
